title: N-Queens
hints: Exactly one queen per row is forced, so the search is: for each row, choose a column that no earlier queen attacks. What three things must be free?
Track the used columns, diagonals (r - c) and anti-diagonals (r + c) in three sets; add before recursing, remove afterwards. Checking a square is then O(1).
count_n_queens is the number of leaves at depth n; solve_n_queens stops at the first leaf (return True up the stack, or use a generator). Bitmasks for the three sets make it very fast.
